title: Three-seed PSRO empirical meta-game feasibility
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A Nash meta-strategy over six heterogeneous historical training policies will retain at least three material support policies, improve training worst-case exposure over uniform/ELO-K5, remain stable across deck seeds, and preserve worst-case performance on three SHA-disjoint holdouts.
material_change: Evaluate a three-seed seat-paired nine-policy greedy payoff matrix and solve the six-policy zero-sum restricted game. No policy weights are trained.
baseline: Current loss-Kbest/ELO-Kbest selectors showed self-family overfit or no robust gain at ~263k hands; uniform and top-row-mean K5 are matched meta-strategy controls.
notes: Primary motivation: Lanctot et al. 2017 PSRO trains approximate best responses to empirical-game meta-strategies; AlphaHoldem instead uses ELO K-best historical policies. This feasibility tests selector geometry only.

Seed0 completed all18432 hands before reporting failed on a 6-weight by9-row holdout matrix dimension error. Payoff gzip recovered as complete 9216 paired rows and exactly skew-symmetric. Recovery slices training rows for mixture scoring and resumes only complete seeds; seed0 is neither regenerated nor overwritten.

Post-run raw audit recovered exactly 9216 paired rows and 36/36 unordered matchups per seed; every matrix had max skew-symmetry error 0 and all gzip SHA256 values matched summary.json. Tests: PSRO 2 passed; full AlphaHoldem suite 296 passed.

result.summary: Completed exactly 55296 frozen greedy seat-paired internal evaluation hands across three deck seeds and nine SHA-distinct policies. The aggregate restricted-game Nash solution collapsed to pure diverse_league5 (support 1, max weight 1.0), while seed1/2 required materially different three-policy mixtures; median seed-to-aggregate weight L1 was 1.5106. Four of seven preregistered gates passed and three failed.
result.conclusion: The present 256-pair-per-matchup empirical matrix is not stable enough to justify a deployable PSRO meta-strategy: aggregate diversity and concentration gates failed and seed weights were unstable. This is a selector-feasibility rejection only, not evidence that PSRO oracle learning or longer-horizon league training fails; this experiment generated zero training hands.
result.next_step: Audit the provenance, learning curve, cross-opponent breadth, seat balance, Standard10 preservation, and external evidence of diverse_league5, which dominated the aggregate training pool. Use that evidence to choose between a higher-confidence matrix/control, a genuine learned best-response PSRO step, or another scalable self-play/league route; scale only a mechanism with reproducible geometric-slope and proxy/external alignment.
